en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn to show which past event happened first. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: had + the third form
steps.text: You know the third form from the present perfect (I've seen, she has finished). Today it comes after had.
steps.body: **Past perfect = had + third form**: *I had finished. She had gone out.* **had** is the same for **every** person: no *has*, no -s. Short form **'d**: *I'd seen* (before a third form, 'd = had, not *would*). Negative: **hadn't** + third form. After had, use the **third form**, not the past: *She had forgot her bag* ✗ → **She had forgotten her bag** ✓; *had went* ✗ → **had gone** ✓. Irregular third forms just have to be remembered.

pairs.en: I had finished.
She had gone out.
We hadn't seen it.
go, went, gone
forget, forgot, forgotten
take, took, taken
leave, left, left

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas has a problem at the office.

question.prompt: Complete: Dimas couldn't call his wife. He had ___ his phone.
question.explanation: After **had** comes the third form: forget → forgot → **forgotten**. 'had forgot' uses the past form, a very common mistake, and 'forget' is the base form.

steps.title: Which happened first?
steps.text: Now the heart of the lesson: two past events, and one small word that changes their order.
steps.body:
Use **had + third form** for the event that happened **first**, when you go back to it in a past story.
**When I arrived, the film had started.** → it started **before** I arrived (I missed the beginning).
**When I arrived, the film started.** → it started **at that moment**.
Indonesian trap: **sudah** in a past story → **had**. *Waktu saya sampai, filmnya sudah mulai* → *the film **had already started*** (not *the film already started*). **already** goes between had and the third form.

pairs.en: When I arrived, the film had started.
pairs.id: Waktu saya sampai, filmnya sudah mulai.

pairs.en: When I arrived, the film started.
had already started
Budi was sad. He had lost his wallet.

steps.title: The film started first
steps.text: Picture the evening at the cinema. Which came first?

timeline.title: When I arrived, the film had started.
timeline.caption: The film started at 7:00: the earlier event → had started. I arrived at 7:15: the later event → arrived. Compare: When I arrived, the film started = I arrived at 7:00 and it started right then.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Bu Ani has an errand at the bank.

question.prompt: The bank closes at 3:00. Bu Ani got there at 3:10. Complete: When Bu Ani got to the bank, it ___.
question.explanation: The bank closed at 3:00, **before** she got there at 3:10 → the earlier event takes had + third form: **had closed**. 'closed' would mean it closed at the moment she arrived, and 'was closing' means it was in the middle of closing.

steps.title: by the time, before, after
steps.text: Three time words help you put past events in order.
steps.body:
**by the time** + past simple → the other part was **already finished** at that moment: *By the time we got to the restaurant, the kitchen **had closed**.*
**before** and **after** already show the order, so the past simple is fine too: *After I **had finished** work, I went home* = *After I **finished** work, I went home.* Both are correct.
With **when**, only the tense shows the order, so choose carefully there.

pairs.en: by the time we got there
pairs.id: saat kami sampai di sana (hal lain sudah terjadi)

pairs.en: By the time we got to the restaurant, the kitchen had closed.
pairs.id: Saat kami sampai di restoran, dapurnya sudah tutup.

pairs.en: After I had finished work, I went home.
After I finished work, I went home.
pairs.id: Setelah selesai kerja, saya pulang. (juga benar)

pairs.en: I had sent the email before my boss called.
pairs.id: Saya sudah mengirim email itu sebelum bos saya menelepon.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: A busy morning at home. Start with By the time.

question.prompt: Arrange the words. Start with By the time: Saat Budi bangun, Rina sudah berangkat.
question.solution: By the time Budi woke up, Rina had left.
question.explanation: **By the time** + past simple (*Budi woke up*), then the event that happened first with had + third form (*Rina had left*): Rina left before Budi woke up. The by the time part comes first, so a comma follows it.

steps.title: Don't overuse it
steps.text: One last rule: had is only for going back in time.
steps.body: Telling **one** past event, or events **in order**? Use the **past simple**. *Yesterday I had gone to the market* ✗ → *Yesterday I **went** to the market* ✓. 'It was long ago' isn't a reason either. Use **had** only when you go **back** to something that happened **before** another past event. (*had a shower* is just the past of *have*.)

examples.en: Yesterday I went to the market.
In 2010 my family moved to Jakarta.
examples.id: Tahun 2010 keluarga saya pindah ke Jakarta. (sudah lama, tetap past simple)

examples.en: I got up, had a shower and went to work.
examples.id: Saya bangun, mandi, lalu berangkat kerja. (berurutan)

examples.en: When I got to work, I noticed I had left my phone at home.
examples.id: Waktu sampai di kantor, saya sadar HP saya tertinggal di rumah. (kembali ke kejadian sebelumnya)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina tells you about her evening.

question.prompt: Rina is talking about one thing she did last night. Choose the correct sentence.
options: Last night I had cooked fried rice for dinner.
Last night I cooked fried rice for dinner.
Last night I have cooked fried rice for dinner.
question.explanation: One past event on its own, with nothing later to go back from → past simple: **cooked**. 'had cooked' needs another, later past event in the story, and 'have cooked' doesn't go with a finished time like last night.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip through these cards: the form, the order, and when not to use it.

flashcards.back: the third form: had gone, had seen, had forgotten (sama untuk semua orang)

flashcards.front: Waktu saya sampai, filmnya sudah mulai.
flashcards.back: When I arrived, the film had already started.

flashcards.front: When I arrived, the film started.
flashcards.back: It started at that moment (filmnya mulai tepat saat saya sampai).
had (already) + third form: When Rina called, I had already eaten.
… had + third form: By the time we got there, the kitchen had closed.
The order is already clear: had finished or finished, both correct.

flashcards.front: Yesterday I had gone to the market. ✗
flashcards.back: Yesterday I went to the market. ✓ (satu kejadian → past simple)

steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · past perfect
artifact.intro: had + third form = the event that happened before another past event.

examples.en: When I got home, my wife had already cooked dinner.
examples.id: Waktu saya sampai di rumah, istri saya sudah memasak makan malam.

examples.en: Budi couldn't open the door because he had lost his key.
examples.id: Budi tidak bisa membuka pintu karena kuncinya hilang.

examples.en: By the time the doctor came, the pain had gone.
examples.id: Saat dokternya datang, rasa sakitnya sudah hilang.

examples.en: Sari cooked dinner before her husband got home.
examples.id: Sari memasak makan malam sebelum suaminya pulang.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar menunjukkan kejadian lampau mana yang terjadi lebih dulu. Ayo kita mulai pelan-pelan.

steps.title: had + bentuk ketiga
steps.text: Kamu sudah kenal bentuk ketiga dari present perfect (I've seen, she has finished). Hari ini bentuk itu muncul setelah had.
steps.body: **Past perfect = had + bentuk ketiga**: *I had finished. She had gone out.* **had** sama untuk **semua** orang: tidak ada *has*, tidak ada -s. Bentuk pendek **'d**: *I'd seen* (sebelum bentuk ketiga, 'd = had, bukan *would*). Negatif: **hadn't** + bentuk ketiga. Setelah had, pakai **bentuk ketiga**, bukan bentuk lampau: *She had forgot her bag* ✗ → **She had forgotten her bag** ✓; *had went* ✗ → **had gone** ✓. Bentuk ketiga yang tidak beraturan memang harus dihafal.

pairs.en: I had finished.
She had gone out.
We hadn't seen it.
go, went, gone
forget, forgot, forgotten
take, took, taken
leave, left, left

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas punya masalah di kantor.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Dimas couldn't call his wife. He had ___ his phone.
question.explanation: Setelah **had** ada bentuk ketiga: forget → forgot → **forgotten**. 'had forgot' memakai bentuk lampau, kesalahan yang sangat sering, dan 'forget' adalah bentuk dasar.

steps.title: Mana yang terjadi lebih dulu?
steps.text: Sekarang inti pelajarannya: dua kejadian lampau, dan satu kata kecil yang mengubah urutannya.
steps.body:
Pakai **had + bentuk ketiga** untuk kejadian yang terjadi **lebih dulu**, saat kamu kembali ke kejadian itu dalam cerita lampau.
**When I arrived, the film had started.** → filmnya mulai **sebelum** saya sampai (saya ketinggalan awalnya).
**When I arrived, the film started.** → filmnya mulai **tepat saat itu**.
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **sudah** dalam cerita lampau → **had**. *Waktu saya sampai, filmnya sudah mulai* → *the film **had already started*** (bukan *the film already started*). **already** diletakkan di antara had dan bentuk ketiga.

pairs.en: When I arrived, the film had started.
pairs.id: Waktu saya sampai, filmnya sudah mulai.

pairs.en: When I arrived, the film started.
had already started
Budi was sad. He had lost his wallet.

steps.title: Filmnya mulai lebih dulu
steps.text: Bayangkan malam itu di bioskop. Mana yang lebih dulu?

timeline.title: When I arrived, the film had started.
timeline.caption: Filmnya mulai jam 7.00: kejadian yang lebih dulu → had started. Saya sampai jam 7.15: kejadian yang belakangan → arrived. Bandingkan: When I arrived, the film started = saya sampai jam 7.00 dan filmnya mulai tepat saat itu.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bu Ani ada urusan di bank.

question.prompt: Bank tutup jam 3.00. Bu Ani sampai di sana jam 3.10. Lengkapi: When Bu Ani got to the bank, it ___.
question.explanation: Bank tutup jam 3.00, **sebelum** dia sampai jam 3.10 → kejadian yang lebih dulu memakai had + bentuk ketiga: **had closed**. 'closed' berarti bank tutup tepat saat dia sampai, dan 'was closing' berarti bank sedang dalam proses tutup.

steps.title: by the time, before, after
steps.text: Tiga kata waktu ini membantumu mengurutkan kejadian lampau.
steps.body:
**by the time** + past simple → bagian yang lain **sudah selesai** pada saat itu: *By the time we got to the restaurant, the kitchen **had closed**.*
**before** (*sebelum*) dan **after** (*setelah*) sudah menunjukkan urutannya, jadi past simple juga boleh: *After I **had finished** work, I went home* = *After I **finished** work, I went home.* Keduanya benar.
Dengan **when**, hanya bentuk kata kerjanya yang menunjukkan urutan, jadi pilih dengan teliti di situ.

pairs.en: by the time we got there
pairs.id: saat kami sampai di sana (hal lain sudah terjadi)

pairs.en: By the time we got to the restaurant, the kitchen had closed.
pairs.id: Saat kami sampai di restoran, dapurnya sudah tutup.

pairs.en: After I had finished work, I went home.
After I finished work, I went home.
pairs.id: Setelah selesai kerja, saya pulang. (juga benar)

pairs.en: I had sent the email before my boss called.
pairs.id: Saya sudah mengirim email itu sebelum bos saya menelepon.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Pagi yang sibuk di rumah. Mulai dengan By the time.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya. Mulai dengan By the time: Saat Budi bangun, Rina sudah berangkat.
question.solution: By the time Budi woke up, Rina had left.
question.explanation: **By the time** + past simple (*Budi woke up*), lalu kejadian yang lebih dulu dengan had + bentuk ketiga (*Rina had left*): Rina berangkat sebelum Budi bangun. Bagian by the time ada di depan, jadi diikuti koma.

steps.title: Jangan berlebihan memakainya
steps.text: Satu aturan terakhir: had hanya untuk kembali ke waktu yang lebih dulu.
steps.body: Menceritakan **satu** kejadian lampau, atau kejadian-kejadian **sesuai urutannya**? Pakai **past simple**. *Yesterday I had gone to the market* ✗ → *Yesterday I **went** to the market* ✓. 'Sudah lama sekali' juga bukan alasan. Pakai **had** hanya kalau kamu kembali ke sesuatu yang terjadi **sebelum** kejadian lampau yang lain. (*had a shower* hanya bentuk lampau dari *have*.)

examples.en: Yesterday I went to the market.
In 2010 my family moved to Jakarta.
examples.id: Tahun 2010 keluarga saya pindah ke Jakarta. (sudah lama, tetap past simple)

examples.en: I got up, had a shower and went to work.
examples.id: Saya bangun, mandi, lalu berangkat kerja. (berurutan)

examples.en: When I got to work, I noticed I had left my phone at home.
examples.id: Waktu sampai di kantor, saya sadar HP saya tertinggal di rumah. (kembali ke kejadian sebelumnya)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina bercerita tentang malamnya.

question.prompt: Rina menceritakan satu hal yang dia lakukan tadi malam. Pilih kalimat yang benar.
options: Last night I had cooked fried rice for dinner.
Last night I cooked fried rice for dinner.
Last night I have cooked fried rice for dinner.
question.explanation: Satu kejadian lampau saja, tanpa kejadian lain yang lebih belakangan → past simple: **cooked**. 'had cooked' butuh kejadian lampau lain yang terjadi setelahnya dalam cerita, dan 'have cooked' tidak cocok dengan waktu yang sudah lewat seperti last night.
